sentences.en: It's been more than 30 years since the height of the HIV-AIDS epidemic began in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国HIV与艾滋病疫情高峰期爆发至今已经过去30多年了。

sentences.en: The survivors of that epidemic are now middle-aged and are still learning how to cope.
sentences.zh: 那场疫情的幸存者如今已到中年，并且仍在学习如何应对。

sentences.en: In the meantime, more effective treatments have changed how the disease is perceived by the public.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，更有效的治疗方法改变了公众对这种疾病的看法。

sentences.en: Perry Haukidis, a psychologist and public health expert, talks in this episode about how psychological science is even more critical
sentences.zh: 心理学家兼公共卫生专家佩里·豪基迪斯在本期节目中谈到，心理科学在以下方面甚至更加至关重要：

sentences.en: in understanding how to prevent HIV and also how to help those who live with all kinds of chronic diseases.
sentences.zh: 不仅要了解如何预防艾滋病，还要了解如何帮助那些身患各种慢性疾病的人。

sentences.en: I'm Audrey Hamilton, and this is Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿，这里是《心理学话语》栏目。

sentences.en: Perry Haukidis is a professor of psychology and global health at New York University.
sentences.zh: 佩里·豪基迪斯是纽约大学心理学和全球卫生教授。

sentences.en: For decades, his work has focused on the intersection of mental health and behavior with HIV prevention and treatment.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，他的工作一直聚焦于心理健康和行为与艾滋病预防和治疗的交叉领域。

sentences.en: His latest book, The AIDS Generation, Stories of Survival and Resilience,
sentences.zh: 他的最新著作《艾滋病一代：生存与韧性的故事》

sentences.en: focuses on 15 gay men who survived the height of the AIDS epidemic and are continuing to live with the disease today.
sentences.zh: 聚焦于15位在艾滋病疫情高峰中幸存下来并至今仍与该疾病共存的男同性恋者。

sentences.en: Dr. Haukidis, welcome.
sentences.zh: 豪基迪斯博士，欢迎您。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Your book talks a lot about the resilience of a generation that saw the worst of the AIDS epidemic.
sentences.zh: 您的书详细谈到了一个经历了艾滋病疫情最黑暗时期的一代人的韧性。

sentences.en: As a psychologist and someone who's living with HIV, it seems very important for you to talk about the mental and emotional impact this disease has had on survivors
sentences.zh: 作为一名心理学家，同时也是一名HIV感染者，对您来说，讨论这种疾病对幸存者造成的心理和情感影响似乎非常重要

sentences.en: who are now in middle age.
sentences.zh: 而他们现在已经步入中年。

sentences.en: Can you tell us more about the people featured in your book and their coping mechanisms?
sentences.zh: 您能多给我们讲讲您书中收录的人物以及他们的应对机制吗？

sentences.en: Are these mechanisms any different from those of people who suffer from other chronic health conditions?
sentences.zh: 这些机制与患有其他慢性健康状况的人所用的机制有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: So the 15 stories that are represented in the book are 15 very different stories.
sentences.zh: 书中呈现的这15个故事是15个截然不同的故事。

sentences.en: I could have told 1,500 stories.
sentences.zh: 我本可以讲述1500个故事。

sentences.en: There was no shortage of them out there.
sentences.zh: 外面从来不缺这样的故事。

sentences.en: But I chose 15 men who came from different walks of life, from different parts of the country, different shapes, sizes, colors,
sentences.zh: 但我选择了15位来自不同背景、来自国家不同地区、身材各异、肤色不同的人，

sentences.en: just to make sure that I captured the diversity of the experience of living with HIV for the last 30 years.
sentences.zh: 只是为了确保我捕捉到了过去30年里与HIV共存这一经历的多元性。

sentences.en: It would be very easy to tell one story, but in fact, HIV is a complicated phenomenon and people dealt with it in many different ways.
sentences.zh: 只讲一个故事会很简单，但事实上，HIV是一个复杂的现象，人们用许多不同的方式来应对它。

sentences.en: So, for example, one of the men in the book became very sick when he was in his early 30s.
sentences.zh: 比如，书中有一位男士在30岁出头时病得很重。

sentences.en: And he is a composer and a piano player.
sentences.zh: 他是一位作曲家和钢琴演奏家。

sentences.en: And he thought all hope was loSt.
sentences.zh: 他曾以为所有的希望都破灭了。

sentences.en: And the way he was able to sort of come out of that was through his music.
sentences.zh: 而他走出阴影的方式是通过他的音乐。

sentences.en: He used his music as a coping mechanism.
sentences.zh: 他将音乐作为一种应对机制。

sentences.en: He talks about how as he was starting to feel better and he would sit at the piano, the music would fill his body again.
sentences.zh: 他谈到，当他开始感觉好点并坐在钢琴前时，音乐再次充满了他的身体。

sentences.en: So, the emotional life that the music gave him revitalized him at a time when there were no effective treatments to actually destroy this virus.
sentences.zh: 因此，音乐赋予他的情感生活在那个实际上没有有效药物来消灭病毒的时代让他重获新生。

sentences.en: And I think that that's a very good example of the role that emotional life and social life plays in fighting this disease.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个很好的例子，说明了情感生活和社会生活在抗击这种疾病中所起的作用。

sentences.en: For a very long time, up to 1996, psychologists and social workers and other clinicians were the support system for living with HIV.
sentences.zh: 在很长一段时间里，直到1996年，心理学家、社会工作者和其他临床医生一直是与HIV共存者的支持系统。

sentences.en: In 1996, everything changed with the advent of medications.
sentences.zh: 1996年，随着药物的出现，一切都变了。

sentences.en: But for a long time, people needed to attend to their emotional and social well-being.
sentences.zh: 但在很长一段时间里，人们需要关注他们的情感和社会福祉。

sentences.en: Other men turned to activism.
sentences.zh: 还有些人转向了激进主义。

sentences.en: One of the characters in the book, Jackson, I call him, became a very, very prominent figure in ACT UP.
sentences.zh: 书中叫杰克逊的这位人物，我称他为杰克逊，成了“联合抗艾行动”（ACT UP）中一个非常非常杰出的人物。

sentences.en: And, you know, people think about ACT UP as an important institution that fought for the development of medications.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们认为ACT UP是一个争取药物研发的重要机构。

sentences.en: And certainly, they did.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们的确做到了。

sentences.en: In the book, I take a slightly different approach in looking at this organization.
sentences.zh: 在这本书中，我在看待这个组织时采用了略有不同的方法。

sentences.en: And for me, what this organization did was that it provided a place for individuals who are living with HIV to come together and support each other and understand each other.
sentences.zh: 对我和这个组织所做的事情而言，它为感染HIV的个人提供了一个聚集在一起、互相支持、互相理解的场所。

sentences.en: And created a social network and social cohesion.
sentences.zh: 并建立了一个社交网络和社会凝聚力。

sentences.en: And we know very clearly from the health psychology literature that that kind of support system leads to better health outcomes.
sentences.zh: 从健康心理学的文献中，我们非常清楚地知道，这种支持系统能带来更好的健康结果。

sentences.en: So, that's two examples.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是两个例子。

sentences.en: The approaches that these men use to dealing with their disease inform how many people deal with their disease if they're doing it in an active, in a proactive way.
sentences.zh: 这些男士用来应对疾病的方法，为许多人如何以积极、前瞻性的方式应对疾病提供了参考。

sentences.en: Which is attending to their physical well-being, their social well-being, and to their emotional well-being.
sentences.zh: 也就是关注他们的身体健康、社交健康和情感健康。

sentences.en: So, the lessons that we can take away from the men of the age generation not only inform the lives of those who are newly infected with HIV,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们可以从“艾滋病一代”的男性身上汲取的经验，不仅能指导新感染HIV的人的生活，

sentences.en: but also individuals who are living with any challenging disease in our society.
sentences.zh: 也能指导我们社会中任何患有具有挑战性疾病的个人的生活。

sentences.en: Now that people are living longer with HIV thanks to effective antiretroviral treatment, what kind of psychological help do they need to cope?
sentences.zh: 既然由于有效的抗逆转录病毒治疗，人们带病生存的时间更长了，他们需要什么样的心理帮助来应对？

sentences.en: You know, are there psychological concerns related to people with HIV knowing that they will have to take, you know, a battery of drugs for the rest of their lives?
sentences.zh: 你知道，感染HIV的人是否会有这样的心理顾虑：他们知道自己在余生中必须服用一连串的药物？

sentences.en: So, the first thing that I would say in response to that question is that HIV is not just a medical condition.
sentences.zh: 因此，我对这个问题给出的第一个回答是，HIV不仅仅是一种医疗状况。

sentences.en: It is a biopsychosocial one.
sentences.zh: 它是一种生物-心理-社会状况。

sentences.en: It is an epidemic that is driven by a virus, but also by emotional and social factors.
sentences.zh: 这是一场由病毒驱动，同时也由情感和社会因素驱动的疫情。

sentences.en: And we can talk about that more fully.
sentences.zh: 我们可以更全面地讨论这一点。

sentences.en: But, with regard to your question specifically, taking a battery of medications is a toll order.
sentences.zh: 但是，就你的具体问题而言，服用一连串药物是一项沉重的负担。

sentences.en: It's no easy task.
sentences.zh: 这不是一件容易的事。

sentences.en: Remembering every day that you're HIV positive when you swallow your pills is burdensome in some ways.
sentences.zh: 每次吞下药丸时，每天都提醒自己是HIV阳性，在某种程度上是一种负担。

sentences.en: As well as individuals live with and accept the fact that they're HIV positive, there's always that peace in their minds that they're living with this chronic disease.
sentences.zh: 尽管个人与HIV阳性的事实共存并接受了它，但他们的脑海中总有那样一个阴影：他们带着这种慢性病生活。

sentences.en: So, psychologists and psychology, which for a very long time was critical in the development of behavioral interventions to fight the spread of this disease, is as important today.
sentences.zh: 因此，在很长一段时间里对开发抗击这种疾病的心理行为干预措施至关重要的心理学家和心理学，在今天同样重要。

sentences.en: What we don't want to happen with this epidemic is to make it purely a biomedical one.
sentences.zh: 我们不希望这场疫情变成纯粹的生物医学问题。

sentences.en: We know that people, yes, they have to take their medications.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，人们是的，他们必须服药。

sentences.en: Yes, they have to go to their doctors.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们必须去看医生。

sentences.en: But they also have a social life and an emotional life that we must attend to.
sentences.zh: 但他们也有我们必须关注的社交生活和情感生活。

sentences.en: And those individuals who will do best in taking their medications every single day, suppressing their virus, remaining healthy, will also be attending to their emotional lives.
sentences.zh: 那些每天按时服药、抑制病毒、保持健康方面做得最好的人，也将是那些关注自己情感生活的人。

sentences.en: They will be getting support from friends and from clinicians and from family members that lift them up to enhance their well-being.
sentences.zh: 他们将从朋友、临床医生和家人那里获得支持，这些支持能振奋他们，提升他们的福祉。

sentences.en: And so, psychology still has as much in my mind to contribute to fighting this epidemic as it did 30 years ago.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我看来，心理学在抗击这场疫情方面的贡献，与30年前一样多。

sentences.en: And I think as psychologists,
sentences.zh: 我认为作为心理学家，

sentences.en: we have been on the forefront and continue to be on the forefront of developing structures and systems and approaches and interventions that speak to the true elements of people's lives.
sentences.zh: 我们一直走在最前沿，并将继续走在开发结构、系统、方法和干预措施的最前沿，这些措施能够反映人们生活的真实要素。

sentences.en: Let's talk a little bit about prevention.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈预防。

sentences.en: You know, people know how HIV is transmitted, yet they still engage in these risky behaviors.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们知道HIV是如何传播的，然而他们仍然在进行这些危险的行为。

sentences.en: You know, how is psychological research and practice helping people change those behaviors?
sentences.zh: 你知道，心理学研究和实践是如何帮助人们改变这些行为的？

sentences.en: So let me start by saying that people just don't wake up one day and say, I'm going to be a risk taker.
sentences.zh: 所以我先说，人们不会有一天醒来就说，我要做一个冒险者。

sentences.en: I'm going to be a drug user.
sentences.zh: 我要成为一个吸毒者。

sentences.en: I'm going to be a meth addict, right?
sentences.zh: 我要成为一个冰毒瘾君子，对吧？

sentences.en: And I think that that's an oversimplification and a dangerous oversimplification.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种过度简化，而且是一种危险的过度简化。

sentences.en: So my work for the last decade has been informed by a theory of syndemics, and that theory is very deeply rooted in psychology.
sentences.zh: 因此，我过去十年的工作一直以协同流行病学（syndemics）理论为指导，而该理论深深植根于心理学。

sentences.en: And here's basically what the theory says.
sentences.zh: 这个理论基本上是这样说的。

sentences.en: Health problems coexiSt.
sentences.zh: 健康问题是共存的。

sentences.en: So where you see mental health problems, you see substance use probleMs.
sentences.zh: 所以你在哪里看到心理健康问题，就会在哪里看到物质使用问题。

sentences.en: Where you see substance use problems, you see sexual risk-taking issues.
sentences.zh: 你在哪里看到物质使用问题，就会在哪里看到性冒险行为问题。

sentences.en: You see other diseases.
sentences.zh: 你会看到其他疾病。

sentences.en: You see obesity.
sentences.zh: 你会看到肥胖症。

sentences.en: You see smoking.
sentences.zh: 你会看到吸烟。

sentences.en: You see all of these things functioning together and in some ways fueling each other.
sentences.zh: 你会看到所有这些东西共同发挥作用，并在某些方面相互助长。

sentences.en: That's one piece of the theory, that health conditions are overlapping.
sentences.zh: 这是该理论的一部分，即健康状况是重叠的。

sentences.en: But the other piece of the theory is that these health conditions are driven by psychosocial burdens.
sentences.zh: 但该理论的另一部分是，这些健康状况是由社会心理负担驱动的。

sentences.en: So individuals who experience discrimination and marginalization because of their race, because of their gender, because of their gender identity,
sentences.zh: 因此，因种族、性别、性别认同而经历歧视和边缘化的个人，

sentences.en: because of their sexual orientation, because of their economic status,
sentences.zh: 因其性取向、经济地位而经历歧视和边缘化的个人，

sentences.en: those individuals are feeling marginalized and experiencing emotional burdens at a much higher rate than others.
sentences.zh: 这些个人感到被边缘化，并承受着比其他人高得多的情感负担。

sentences.en: Those emotional burdens in some ways engender the risk that people engage in because the risk is a coping mechanism for the realities of people's lives.
sentences.zh: 这些情感负担在某种程度上催生了人们所从事的冒险行为，因为冒险行为是应对人们生活现实的一种应对机制。

sentences.en: So psychology is still really critical in understanding why HIV continues to exist in our country.
sentences.zh: 因此，在理解为什么HIV在我国依然存在方面，心理学仍然至关重要。

sentences.en: When you think about who is affected by the disease, primarily gained by sexual men, primarily gained by sexual men of color, African-American women.
sentences.zh: 当你想到受该疾病影响的人群时，主要是男男性行为者，主要是男性的有色人种同性恋者，非洲裔美国女性。

sentences.en: And these are segments, these individuals are members of segments of our population that are continuing to be marginalized.
sentences.zh: 这些群体、这些个人是我们人口中持续被边缘化的群体的成员。

sentences.en: And until we establish an equal playing field where all people have, you know, are treated the same way, that have the same rights, that have access to affordable,
sentences.zh: 在我们建立一个公平的竞技场之前——在这里所有人，你知道的，都受到平等的对待，拥有相同的权利，能够获得负担得起的、

sentences.en: good health care, we're going to continue to see this epidemic lodging itself in those groups that are experiencing the most discrimination.
sentences.zh: 良好的医疗保健，我们将继续看到这场疫情盘踞在那些经历最多歧视的群体中。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about the introduction of Truvada, then.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我们来谈谈特鲁瓦达（Truvada）的推出。

sentences.en: You know, this is the drug that has been shown to reduce the risk of contracting HIV.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是已被证明能降低感染HIV风险的药物。

sentences.en: You know, what impact do you think it's having or will have on the arc of the HIV-AIDS epidemic?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你认为它对HIV/AIDS疫情的发展轨迹正在产生或将要产生什么影响？

sentences.en: You know, particularly among young people, some of these groups that you're talking about, who have grown up being constantly warned about the dangers of unprotected sex.
sentences.zh: 你知道，特别是在年轻人当中，在你所说的这些群体中，他们从小就被不断警告无保护性行为的危险。

sentences.en: So Truvada, as we know, is one of the HIV medications that is used for people who are living with the virus,
sentences.zh: 所以特鲁瓦达，正如我们所知，是用于携带病毒者的HIV药物之一，

sentences.en: which has been shown in trials to be effective in preventing the onset of HIV.
sentences.zh: 临床试验表明它在预防HIV发作方面是有效的。

sentences.en: So if you take one Truvada once a day and engage in risk behaviors and are exposed to HIV, it is highly likely that you will not become infected because of this drug.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你每天服用一次特鲁瓦达，并从事危险行为并暴露于HIV，由于这种药物，你极有可能不会被感染。

sentences.en: When the drug is used that way, it's called pre-exposure prophylaxis or PrEP.
sentences.zh: 当这种药物以这种方式使用时，它被称为暴露前预防或PrEP。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's great, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，这太棒了，对吧？

sentences.en: Here's the problem.
sentences.zh: 问题来了。

sentences.en: Well, let me stop there and step back and say, here's the plus.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我停下来退一步说，好处在这里。

sentences.en: The plus is we have another tool in the arsenal to fight HIV.
sentences.zh: 好处是我们有了抗击HIV的又一个工具。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: We'll take PrEP.
sentences.zh: 我们用PrEP。

sentences.en: We'll combine it with clinical approaches.
sentences.zh: 我们将它与临床方法结合起来。

sentences.en: We'll combine it with behavioral interventions.
sentences.zh: 我们将它与行为干预结合起来。

sentences.en: We'll continue to do the work that we're doing.
sentences.zh: 我们将继续做我们正在做的工作。

sentences.en: So one more tool, a good tool.
sentences.zh: 所以又多了一个工具，一个好工具。

sentences.en: But this goes back to the point I raised earlier, which is we cannot think about this disease as purely a biomedical one, right?
sentences.zh: 但这回到了我之前提出的观点，即我们不能把这种疾病看作是纯粹的生物医学问题，对吧？

sentences.en: So taking one pill once a day sounds like a great idea, but we know that HIV-positive people have trouble taking their medications every day.
sentences.zh: 所以一天吃一次药听起来是个好主意，但我们知道HIV阳性的人每天按时服药都有困难。

sentences.en: Why are we to believe that HIV-negative people who are not living with the virus are going to take their medications every day?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们要相信没有感染病毒的HIV阴性的人会每天吃药呢？

sentences.en: So while PrEP provides a situation for us and an opportunity for us to fight the virus on another
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然PrEP为我们提供了一个在另一个

sentences.en: front, it has to be coupled with effective behavioral approaches that support taking the medication
sentences.zh: 阵地上抗击病毒的情境和机会，但它必须与支持服药的有效行为方法相结合，

sentences.en: and with messaging and education from our community, from our governments, from our religious leaders
sentences.zh: 并与来自我们社区、我们的政府、我们的宗教领袖的信息和教育相结合，

sentences.en: that HIV is a disease that is very much part of our reality and should not be stigmatized.
sentences.zh: 即HIV是一种深深嵌入我们现实生活中的疾病，不应受到污名化。

sentences.en: And so I hope that we can nest PrEP within a larger framework of HIV prevention and care that thinks about physical, emotional, and social well-beings of individuals.
sentences.zh: 因此，我希望我们能将PrEP置于一个更广泛的HIV预防和护理框架内，考虑到个人的身体、情感和社会福祉。

sentences.en: And you mentioned the stigma surrounding people who are HIV-positive.
sentences.zh: 你提到了围绕HIV阳性人群的污名化。

sentences.en: It still is a very serious concern and a barrier to care.
sentences.zh: 这仍然是一个非常严重的问题，也是获得护理的障碍。

sentences.en: What should psychology do to help overcome this stigma?
sentences.zh: 心理学应该做些什么来帮助克服这种污名化？

sentences.en: Is it possible?
sentences.zh: 这可能吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's amazing to me as a 51-year-old man now who saw the height of the epidemic and all of the pain and suffering of the 80s if the stigma still exists.
sentences.zh: 是的，作为一个现在51岁、经历过疫情高峰以及80年代所有痛苦与苦难的男人，如果这种污名化依然存在，这让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: And I was reminded of it recently when I saw the reaction to the Ebola epidemic and how people were terrified and, you know, being hospitalized for no reason.
sentences.zh: 我最近从看到对埃博拉疫情的反应中想到了这一点，人们是多么惊慌失措，你知道的，无缘无故地被住院隔离。

sentences.en: Entering the country became more difficult.
sentences.zh: 入境国家变得更加困难。

sentences.en: This was just, it raised all those emotions for me around what the 80s looked like, you know, where people were completely panicked.
sentences.zh: 这简直是，它唤起了我关于80年代是什么样子的所有那些情绪，你知道的，当时人们完全陷入了恐慌。

sentences.en: So stigma around HIV is very much still there.
sentences.zh: 所以围绕HIV的污名化确实依然存在。

sentences.en: Some people still think HIV as a disease of gay people and of drug users.
sentences.zh: 有些人仍然认为HIV是同性恋者和吸毒者的疾病。

sentences.en: And in fact, we know that it's not that.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们知道并非如此。

sentences.en: It affects every segment of our population.
sentences.zh: 它影响着我们人口的每一个阶层。

sentences.en: But because of its historic roots and because sometimes more narrow-minded individuals use it as an opportunity to further marginalize some groups, stigma still exists.
sentences.zh: 但由于其历史根源，以及有时思想更狭隘的人利用它作为进一步边缘化某些群体的机会，污名化依然存在。

sentences.en: So psychology is critically important in helping to undermine stigma that exists in our society.
sentences.zh: 因此，心理学对于帮助消除我们社会中存在的污名化至关重要。

sentences.en: And we have to remember one more thing, that people who might experience stigma because of HIV might be experiencing stigmas for many other reasons,
sentences.zh: 我们还必须记住一件事，那就是可能因HIV而经历污名化的人，可能由于许多其他原因正在经历污名化，

sentences.en: because they're gay, because they're black, because they're poor, because they're from a certain neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 因为他们是同性恋，因为他们是黑人，因为他们贫穷，因为他们来自某个特定的社区。

sentences.en: And so what psychology continues to need to do is to continue to message to people how it is that we expect to treat others,
sentences.zh: 因此，心理学需要继续做的事情是，继续向人们传达我们期望如何对待他人，

sentences.en: to message to those who are living with the burdens and with the stigma, that it is okay to be vocal and to express one's feelings and ideas when one is being marginalized,
sentences.zh: 向那些承受负担和污名化的人传达，在被边缘化时，直言不讳、表达自己的感受和想法是没有问题的，

sentences.en: to continue to train psychologists for the future, to work in hospitals and in schools, to teach people about the damaging effects of discrimination and marginalization.
sentences.zh: 继续培养未来的心理学家，让他们在医院和学校工作，教导人们认识歧视和边缘化带来的破坏性影响。

sentences.en: And I think that only psychology can do that.
sentences.zh: 我认为只有心理学才能做到这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, psychology is really critical in helping us advance how we think about issues like marriage equality.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，心理学对于帮助我们推进对婚姻平等之类问题的思考真的至关重要。

sentences.en: You know, psychology was really critical, you know, in the 1960s when interracial marriage was a complex issue for some people.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在20世纪60年代跨种族婚姻对某些人来说是一个复杂问题时，心理学真的很关键。

sentences.en: And so we take the lessons from psychology that we've learned over the last hundred plus years
sentences.zh: 因此，我们将从过去一百多年里从心理学中学到的经验教训

sentences.en: and apply them to HIV, which is provide supports to people who are living with the virus to empower them, work to educate a new generation,
sentences.zh: 应用到HIV上，即为感染病毒的人提供支持以赋予他们力量，努力教育新一代，

sentences.en: normalize HIV in our society so that the stigma eventually dissipates.
sentences.zh: 在我们的社会中使HIV正常化，以便污名最终消散。

sentences.en: Thank you, Dr. Halkidis.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，豪基迪斯博士。

sentences.en: This has been a very interesting conversation.
sentences.zh: 这是一次非常有趣的对话。

sentences.en: I appreciate you taking the time.
sentences.zh: 感谢您抽出时间。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: You can check out Halkidis' work and his latest book on our website,
sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站上查看豪基迪斯的工作和他的最新著作，

sentences.en: speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: speakingofpsychology.org.

sentences.zh: 欢迎来到美国心理学协会，说到心理学，

sentences.zh: 我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿。
